source_discovery.function_contract_metadata: supported via kani_metadata::KaniMetadata::contracted_functions; source file and proof-for-contract harness identities are preserved as planning provenance with proof_credit=false

statements: for _ in LITERAL..LITERAL with at most 32 iterations
expressions: +, -, * only inside executable if conditions; Verus must discharge fixed-width overflow/underflow
accepted.loops: literal ranges are exhaustively unrolled; this is not a general loop invariant or recursion theorem
accepted.assumptions: preserved at their source program point; for each user assumption, Verus proves that every otherwise feasible non-arithmetic path prefix retains at least one fixed-width input after the assumption
accepted.machine_arithmetic: Kani uses checked Rust overflow semantics at the pinned revision; translated +,-,* remain in executable Verus if conditions, where Verus requires overflow/underflow absence. Ghost arithmetic is rejected, and arithmetic-dependent assumption reachability is rejected rather than widened.
accepted.generics: source functions with unbounded type parameters only when Kani autoharness selected an explicit monomorphic instance and every selected type is in the supported fixed-width integer/Boolean set; the result is scoped to that concrete instantiation
accepted.function_contract_discovery: Kani compiler metadata for contracted functions is preserved and validated end-to-end so the Verus planner can see exact function/file/harness provenance without reimplementing Kani discovery

rejected: requires/ensures/modifies expression translation and contract proof semantics; contract metadata discovery alone is not a Verus contract proof
arithmetic in assert!/kani::assume, division/remainder, casts, arithmetic outside executable if conditions, and assumption non-vacuity paths that depend on machine arithmetic
references, raw pointers, slices, allocation and user ADTs
concurrency in the generated-source translator; reviewed Kani-selected functions may still bind to the separate existing Verus concurrency campaign through registry.json
generic trait-bound syntax, const generics, lifetimes, target-width generic arguments, dynamic loops, named loop variables and recursion
semantic_bridge.translation_trust: Structural lowering is an explicit trusted correspondence boundary and is regression-tested. Scoped assumptions are guarded by Verus-checked path-preservation non-vacuity obligations; syntactically unreachable assertion branches are recorded but are not required to have witnesses. Kani function-contract metadata is preserved as provenance only until contract expressions receive an explicit semantic bridge. No general Rust-to-Verus translation soundness is claimed.
